tasks.title: Engine Service Core + Auth + Health
tasks.description: Create engine_service.py with FastAPI app skeleton, CORS middleware, token authentication (Authorization: Token <secret> — NOT Bearer; via ENGINE_TOKEN env var, no hardcoded default), Pydantic request/response models for all 8 endpoints, consistent error response format, structured request logging, and GET /health endpoint. Include SIGTERM handler that sets a shutdown flag and allows in-flight requests to drain. CLI args: --port (default 3082), --token (default from ENGINE_TOKEN env). Port-conflict detection on startup.
acceptance_criteria: FastAPI app starts on 0.0.0.0:3082 with CORS enabled
Token auth (Authorization: Token <secret> — NOT Bearer) rejects requests without valid Authorization header
GET /health returns {status, uptime, model, gpu_temp} within 5s
Pydantic models defined for all endpoint request/response types
Consistent error response: {error: str, detail: str, status_code: int}
SIGTERM triggers graceful shutdown (finish in-flight, then exit)
Structured JSON logging for every request (method, path, status, duration)
Port conflict returns clear error message on startup

tasks.title: Inference Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement POST /inference endpoint that proxies chat completion requests to BeeLlama. Accept {port: int, messages: list, max_tokens: int, temperature: float, top_p: float, top_k: int}. Forward to BeeLlama at the correct port (8080 for 3090, 8082 for 3070). 300s timeout to handle long thinking. Return {content, reasoning, timings, usage}. Handle BeeLlama unavailability with 503 + retry hint. Update service state to PROCESSING during inference, back to READY on completion.
acceptance_criteria: POST /inference accepts valid BeeLlama request payload
Proxies to correct BeeLlama port (8080 or 8082) based on port param
300s timeout allows long-running inference (30-60s thinking)
Response includes content, reasoning_content, timings, usage
503 returned when BeeLlama is unreachable
Service state transitions: READY → PROCESSING → READY
Handles malformed messages list with 422 validation error

tasks.title: File Operations Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement POST /write-files endpoint. Accept {project_path: str, files: [{path: str, content: str}]}. Write each file atomically (write to temp, rename). Collect errors per file. Return {written: list, errors: list, bytes_total: int}. Validate project_path exists and is under allowed directories. Reject path traversal (../) in file paths.
acceptance_criteria: POST /write-files writes all files to specified project_path
Atomic writes: file content written via temp+rename pattern
Path traversal (../) rejected with 400 error
Non-existent project_path returns 404 with clear error
Partial failures collected: written list has successes, errors list has failures
bytes_total accurately reflects total bytes written
Empty files list returns {written: [], errors: [], bytes_total: 0}

tasks.title: Test Runner + Git Commit Endpoints
tasks.description: Implement POST /run-tests: accept {project_path: str, pattern: str}, run pytest subprocess with timeout 120s, parse JUnit XML or stdout, return {status: str, passed: int, failed: int, results: list}. Implement POST /git-commit: accept {project_path: str, message: str, files: list}, run git add + git commit, return {sha: str, message: str}. Both use subprocess with proper timeout and error capture.
acceptance_criteria: POST /run-tests executes pytest in project_path with pattern filter
Test results parsed: passed/failed counts + per-test status
120s timeout kills long-running test suites gracefully
POST /git-commit stages specified files and commits with message
Commit SHA returned in response
Non-git directory returns 400 with clear error
Empty files list in git-commit returns 400 (nothing to commit)

tasks.title: Exec + GPU Status + SSE Streaming Endpoints
tasks.description:
Implement POST /exec: accept {command: str, cwd: str, timeout: int}, execute shell command, return {stdout, stderr, rc}. Restrict dangerous commands (rm -rf /, etc.) or require --allow-exec flag. Implement GET /gpu-status: query nvidia-smi, return {gpus: [{index, name, temp, vram_used, vram_total, util}]}. Implement GET /stream: SSE endpoint with query params ?channels=engine,gpu, periodic heartbeat (30s keepalive), event format: event: <channel>
data: <json>
acceptance_criteria: POST /exec runs shell command with configurable timeout
Dangerous commands blocked or warnlogged (rm -rf, mkfs, etc.)
GET /gpu-status returns per-GPU metrics from nvidia-smi
GET /stream establishes SSE connection with correct Content-Type
SSE heartbeat sent every 30s to prevent proxy/client timeout
Channel filtering: only events for requested channels are sent
exec timeout returns partial stdout/stderr + timeout error

tasks.title: Engine HTTP Client
tasks.description: Create engine_client.py with EngineClient class that mirrors the LocalTransport/RemoteTransport API. Uses urllib.request (stdlib) for zero dependencies. Features: connection reuse, configurable base_url and token, request timeout per-endpoint, retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts, 1s/2s/4s), structured error handling (EngineClientError). Methods: inference(), write_files(), run_tests(), git_commit(), exec_command(), health(), gpu_status(), stream(). All methods return parsed JSON dicts.
acceptance_criteria: EngineClient class with all 8 endpoint methods
Zero external dependencies (stdlib urllib only)
Token auth via Authorization: Token <secret> header (NOT Bearer)
Retry with exponential backoff: 3 attempts, delays 1s/2s/4s
Connection reuse via urllib connection pooling
Per-endpoint timeout configuration
EngineClientError exception class with status_code and response body
Methods return parsed JSON dicts matching API response schemas
stream() returns an iterator of SSE events

tasks.title: HTTPTransport + Transport Selection Logic
tasks.description: Add HTTPTransport class to transport.py that wraps EngineClient and mirrors LocalTransport/RemoteTransport API (curl_beellama, run_command, check_beellama_health, get_model_list, nvidia_smi, run_git, docker_exec, docker_run). Update get_transport() with new priority: (1) HTTP — probe GET /health on port 3082, (2) Local — BeeLlama reachable at localhost, (3) SSH — RemoteTransport fallback. Include transport fallback: if HTTP request fails with ConnectionError, log warning and fall back to SSH for that request. Cache transport selection but allow forced override via TRANSPORT_MODE env var.
acceptance_criteria: HTTPTransport class implements same API surface as LocalTransport/RemoteTransport
get_transport() tries HTTP first (probe localhost:3082/health)
Fallback chain: HTTP → Local → SSH
TRANSPORT_MODE env var can force: 'http', 'local', 'ssh', or 'auto'
HTTPTransport falls back to SSH on ConnectionError
Transport selection logged at startup
Existing code (code_generator, test_runner, git_workflow) works without changes
HTTPTransport handles 503 from engine service gracefully

tasks.title: CLI Commands + Service Lifecycle State Machine
tasks.description: Add engine subcommand group to harness.py: 'engine start [--port] [--token]', 'engine stop', 'engine status'. 'engine start' launches engine_service.py as background process, writes PID file. 'engine stop' sends SIGTERM via PID file. 'engine status' queries GET /health and displays service state. Implement full service lifecycle state machine: STOPPED → STARTING → READY → PROCESSING → DEGRADED → FAILED, persisted in a .state file. State transitions: startup health check → READY, inference request → PROCESSING, inference complete → READY, repeated errors → DEGRADED, max failures → FAILED.
acceptance_criteria: harness.py engine start launches service as background process
PID file written for stop/status commands
harness.py engine stop sends SIGTERM gracefully
harness.py engine status shows service health + uptime + state
State machine: STOPPED → STARTING → READY → PROCESSING → DEGRADED → FAILED
State persisted in .state file for crash recovery
Consecutive error count tracked; 5+ errors → DEGRADED, 10+ → FAILED
Engine start fails gracefully if port is already in use

tasks.title: Systemd Unit + SSH Fallback Fixes
tasks.description: Create engine_service.unit systemd unit file: Type=simple, Restart=always, RestartSec=5, Environment=ENGINE_TOKEN, EnvironmentFile=-/etc/engine-token. Also fix SSH fallback in transport.py: (1) Remove hardcoded password '12345', use SSH key auth only, (2) Add ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPath=/tmp/ssh-engine-%r@%h:%p for connection pooling, (3) Increase SSH timeout to 300s for inference calls, (4) Add ServerAliveInterval=30 ServerAliveCountMax=10 for keepalive.
acceptance_criteria: systemd unit file starts engine_service.py with correct env
Restart=always with RestartSec=5 for auto-recovery
EnvironmentFile supports token from /etc/engine-token
SSH uses key auth only (no sshpass dependency)
SSH ControlMaster=auto for connection pooling
SSH timeout increased to 300s for inference
SSH keepalive: ServerAliveInterval=30, ServerAliveCountMax=10
No hardcoded passwords in any file

tasks.title: Integration + Resilience Tests
tasks.description: Create test_engine_service.py with: (1) Unit tests for all 8 endpoints using httpx TestClient, (2) Integration test: POST inference → verify response → POST write-files → verify file on disk → POST run-tests → verify results → POST git-commit → verify SHA, (3) Resilience test: kill service mid-inference, verify client retries and falls back to SSH, (4) Transport selection test: mock each environment and verify correct transport returned, (5) Auth test: verify token validation, (6) Concurrent request test: 5 parallel inference requests, no drops.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 endpoints have request/response validation tests
Integration test completes full write→test→commit pipeline
Resilience test: service kill → client retry → SSH fallback works
Transport selection returns HTTP when service is up
Transport selection returns SSH when service is down
Auth: missing token → 401, wrong token → 403, valid token → 200
5 concurrent requests complete without drops or errors
All tests runnable with: python3 -m pytest test_engine_service.py

metadata.iteration_1_summary: Initial decomposition into 9 atomic tasks covering API endpoints, client, transport, and deployment. Each task scoped to <50 LOC where possible.

MISSING: Structured error response format (consistent {error, detail, status_code}) — added to T01
MISSING: Request logging (method, path, status, duration) — added to T01
SECURITY: POST /exec allows arbitrary command execution — added dangerous command blocking in T05
MISSING: SSE heartbeat/keepalive (30s interval) to prevent proxy timeouts — added to T05
MISSING: Connection pooling in HTTP client — added to T06
MISSING: Retry with exponential backoff in HTTP client — added to T06 (3 attempts, 1s/2s/4s)
MISSING: Transport fallback (HTTP fails → SSH for that request) — added to T07
MISSING: SSH Tier 1 fixes (sshpass removal, key auth, ControlMaster, timeouts) — added to T09
MISSING: Port conflict detection on startup — added to T01
DEPENDENCY ERROR: T09 (CLI) needed T08 (transport) for status display — fixed ordering
MISSING: Integration and resilience tests — added T10
SECURITY: Hardcoded default token 'engine-secret-2024' — changed to require ENGINE_TOKEN env var
MISSING: State machine state persistence for crash recovery — added .state file to T08
iteration_3_finalizations: Added service lifecycle state machine: STOPPED → STARTING → READY → PROCESSING → DEGRADED → FAILED
Added transport selection state machine: HTTP? → Local? → SSH fallback
Added error handling: consistent Pydantic validation errors, HTTP error responses, exception chaining
Added retry policy: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) on ConnectionError/503
Added graceful shutdown: SIGTERM → drain in-flight requests → exit (max 30s drain timeout)
Added request logging: structured JSON with method, path, status_code, duration_ms
Added SSE heartbeat: 30s keepalive comment events to prevent proxy timeouts
Added dangerous command blocking for /exec endpoint
Added state persistence via .state file for crash recovery
parallelization_opportunities: T02, T03, T04, T05 can be implemented in parallel (all depend only on T01)
T09 and T10 are independent of each other but both depend on T08
